title: How to Choose Medical Interpreting Services
summary: Weigh on-site, OPI, VRI, and AI medical interpreting services by cost, speed, and clinical fit to meet Title VI standards. September 2026.
body_markdown:
###


AI medical interpretation connects in seconds across 150+ languages with no billed silence and integrates directly into EHR and telehealth workflows, making it a strong first-line choice for most encounters. Over-the-phone interpreting remains a reliable escalation path when a patient requests a human interpreter or organizational policy requires one. Build your routing logic around encounter urgency, language availability, and patient preference instead of defaulting to a single modality.


###


Opalite Health supports 150+ languages and dialects through real-time AI interpretation; NoBarrier covers roughly 45 languages through AI (with additional coverage through human interpreters); and Lexi supports approximately 35+ languages through AI, making Opalite one of the broadest AI-native medical interpretation options available to healthcare organizations today. Coverage depth matters most for rare-language requests and after-hours encounters where human interpreter queues slow down. Confirm dialect-level support for your specific patient population before signing any contract.


###


Section 1557 requires meaningful access for patients with limited English proficiency but does not mandate a specific modality, so validated AI interpretation with quality guardrails can satisfy the standard alongside qualified human interpreters. Your organization owns the approved use cases, patient disclosure process, escalation pathways, and quality monitoring program. Opalite Guardian pairs automated safety checks with human-supported review of protected encounter data to support that compliance program.


###


Judge vendors on cost per completed encounter instead of the headline per-minute rate, and audit for billed silent minutes and rare-language surcharges, which are where language access budgets quietly erode. Beyond pricing, confirm independent clinical validation, BAA availability, PHI handling practices, EHR integration depth, and escalation pathways between AI, VRI, OPI, and on-site interpreters. An independent validation study, such as the Johns Hopkins Medicine study Opalite completed, gives procurement and compliance teams concrete evidence to weigh instead of marketing assertions.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation with documented quality controls, encounter logging, patient disclosure, and clear escalation pathways is appropriate across a broad range of clinical settings, including complex consent discussions. Your organization sets the approved use cases and escalation triggers, such as low-confidence output or patient request for a human interpreter. Governance setup, not modality selection, is what determines whether any interpretation method meets your clinical and compliance standards.
